author: Bijan Mousavi
title: Retained reports and exact generated integration nodes
why: Parent-bound report evidence must survive fork PR merges without silently admitting unreported merge changes.
what: Add original-tree report/history reproduction and a narrow GitHub integration validator for checked parents, PR provenance, expected merge trees and live Actions identities.
how: Reject wrong parents, missing or stale reports, unreported merge changes, conflicting trees, foreign PRs and failed/pending/skipped checks. Reproduce historical reports with each original renderer.
preserved: Original authored commits, parent/payload bindings and archived triplet bytes remain intact. Generated merge nodes get external check/provenance evidence; authored resolutions still require normal reports.
risk: Historical contributor tools/TeX must run in disposable secret-free environments. Local check indexes are not trusted as live outcomes; the integration CLI queries Actions and downloads checkout identities.
limitations: 105 tooling tests pass. All nine prior reports reproduce byte-identically with their original tools in this environment. Synthetic merge probes are unit controls, not actual GitHub merges or approval. Bootstrap workflow execution and first permanent merge remain pending.
rollback: Revert integration tools and documentation together in a reported commit. Retain authored evidence and require a verified replacement protocol before further merge operations.
